'''Jens Westphalen''' (born 1964 in [[Hamburg]]) is a German wildlife [[filmmaker]], [[Film director|director]] and [[film producer]]. His documentaries have received many awards.
[[File:Jens_Westphalen_filming_wildlife_in_the_forests_of_Borneo.jpg|thumb|Jens Westphalen while filming in Borneo, 2018]]

== Life and career ==
Jens Westphalen grew up in [[Langenhorn, Hamburg|Hamburg-Langenhorn]]. During his childhood and youth he was interested in animals and nature, photography and film. This also led to his early desire to become a wildlife filmmaker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brocken |first=Interview: R. Otto |date=2012-07-09 |title="Ich wollte schon als Kind Naturfilmer werden" |url=https://www.shz.de/lokales/niebuell-leck/artikel/ich-wollte-schon-als-kind-naturfilmer-werden-41387830 |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=shz.de |language=de}}</ref> After graduating from high school in Heidberg, Jens Westphalen traveled through South America for a year and gained his first experiences as a professional photographer. Jens Westphalen then did community service and then studied biology at the University of Hamburg.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.hoerzu.de/wissen/tierfilmer/ | title=Tierfilmer*innen bei der Arbeit: Die erstaunlichsten Momente | date=26 November 2021 }}</ref> Jens Westphalen then worked as a nature photographer in Africa, Asia, Europe and South America, mainly during the semester breaks. While studying biology, Jens Westphalen met his fellow student Thoralf Grospitz. He began making his first nature films with him before he finished his studies. They later founded the production company Zorillafilm. Animal and nature films such as ''Die Nordsee'' (''The North Sea''), ''Wildes Japan'' (''Wild Japan'') and the ''Australien'' (''Australia'') series have been made since 1993. The documentaries portray natural areas such as "Poland's East", "Borneo's Secret Kingdom" and "Wild Hamburg" or animal species such as African elephants, dingoes, red kangaroos and sea turtles. But Jens Westphalen is not only taken with large and exotic animals: in 2003 the film ''Die frechen Spatzen von Berlin'' (''The Cheeky Sparrows of Berlin'') was made.

In addition to various European countries, these include: Costa Rica, India, Sri Lanka, New Zealand, Australia, Borneo, Namibia, Zambia, Botswana and Japan are Jens Westphalen's filming locations. On his film trips he usually travels for months and often in remote areas with his film partner Thoralf Grospitz.
[[File:Jens_Westphalen_and_Thoralf_Grospitz_surrounded_by_elephants_in_Botswana.jpg|thumb|Jens Westphalen and Thoralf Grospitz with elefants, Botswana, 2017]]
Numerous documentaries have received nominations and awards at international film festivals and television awards. In 2011, the two-parter ''Wild Japan'' received a nomination for Best Documentary at the International Emmy Award.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sewig |first=Claudia |date=2011-11-15 |title=Zwei Hamburger Naturfilmer für den Emmy nominiert |url=https://www.abendblatt.de/vermischtes/article108170931/Zwei-Hamburger-Naturfilmer-fuer-den-Emmy-nominiert.html |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=www.abendblatt.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=NDR.de |title=NDR Produktionen "Allein gegen die Zeit" und "Wildes Japan" für Emmy nominiert |url=https://www.ndr.de/der_ndr/presse/mitteilungen/ndr-produktionen-allein-gegen-die-zeit-und-wildes-japan-fuer-emmy-nominiert,pressemeldungndr9027.html |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=ndr.de |language=de}}</ref> Other films also received honors: For example, the film ''Australien – im Reich der Riesenkängurus'' (''Australia – in the realm of the giant kangaroos'') won the Deutschen Naturfilmpreis (German Nature Film Prize),<ref name="ndr.de">{{cite web | url=https://www.ndr.de/der_ndr/presse/mitteilungen/Deutscher-Naturfilmpreis-fuer-NDRARTE-Koproduktion-Australien-Im-Reich-der-Riesenkaengurus,pressemeldungndr14796.html | title=Deutscher Naturfilmpreis für NDR/ARTE-Koproduktion "Australien - Im Reich der Riesenkängurus" }}</ref> the "Best Camera" award at the Green Screen Nature Film Festival, "Best Film" at the Animal Behavior Society<ref name="ndr.de"/> and the "Grand Prix" at the [[Matsalu International Nature Film Festival]]. Films have also received awards at the [[New York Festivals]] several times. Jens Westphalen is therefore one of the most renowned German nature filmmakers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sewig |first=Claudia |date=2010-09-07 |title=Diese Hamburger zählen zu den besten Naturfilmern Deutschlands |url=https://www.abendblatt.de/hamburg/article107848449/Diese-Hamburger-zaehlen-zu-den-besten-Naturfilmern-Deutschlands.html |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=www.abendblatt.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.greenscreen-festival.de/festival/regisseure/detail/westphalen | title=Detail | date=9 July 2024 }}</ref>

Jens Westphalen and his film partner Thoralf Grospitz have established themselves on the international television market with their productions and work together with television stations and production companies such as [[ARD (broadcaster)|ARD]], [[ZDF]], NDR, WDR, BR, [[Arte]], ORF, [[Deutsche Welle]], NDR Naturfilm Doclights, [[National Geographic Channel]], [[Terra Mater Factual Studios]] and Wildbear Entertainment.

Jens Westphalen's documentaries are shown in Germany, among others, in the ARD series Erlebnis Erde (Experience Earth) and in the NDR series [[:de:Expeditionen ins Tierreich|Expeditionen ins Tierreich]](Expeditions into the Animal Kingdom). He also worked for the children's series [[Die Sendung mit der Maus]] (The Show with the Mouse) and [[Löwenzahn]] (Dandelion).

Jens Westphalen lives with his family in Hamburg.
